context:
Goal: no reviewed PR waits, and a tool, not a hand, keeps it so.
Problem (goal): PRs are made about 7 times faster than they merge. Lanes find gaps, each gap becomes a new lane, and the batch runner builds each batch by hand. You called the hold options bandaids (21:44 CST).
Based on (notes): the coordinator counts about 380 PRs opened (#1384 to #1763) against 26 batches of 1-5 lanes.
Based on (notes): root cause found by runner 8: a coordinator handoff line with no ruling, "a guard or check change batches alone", put most done PRs one per batch, at 21-37 min of CI each. The coordinator withdrew it at 21:46 CST. Runner 8 now batches every clean done PR together and builds the next batch while one runs.
Departs from: main, where each finding becomes its own step and lane, and the runner builds each batch by hand from messages — the merge tool batches every reviewed PR itself, and a lane's findings ride in its own PR or one follow-up per topic.
Meanwhile: your hold on new lanes stays, except lanes that land these fixes.

options.gain: Merges keep pace with reviews, finding PRs stop multiplying, and a stall shows in the counts.
options.how: (1) The merge tool builds each batch from PR state: every PR with a done review record on its live head and a lane lint pass. It splits a red batch itself, and builds the next batch while one runs, on top of #1561's ledger. (2) A lane's findings join its next commit, or one follow-up PR per topic. (3) Every runner and coordinator report gives three counts: reviewed PRs waiting past one batch cycle, open PRs with no next act, and finished lanes not archived. A count not read says unknown.
options.label: All three parts (recommended)
options.lose: Two process changes and one large merge-tool lane. Findings land bundled.

options.gain: One change, and the queue drains.
options.label: Part 1 only: the merge tool builds batches
Part 2 only: findings ride in their lane

ref: steps pr-backlog-clear and pr-state-is-on-the-pr; #1561 (the PR ledger)
title: Make merges keep pace with reviews: which parts?
why: The coordinator recommends a: part 1 alone drains the queue but does not slow new PRs, and part 2 alone does not drain it.
